title: The Trial Over Ahmaud Arbery's Killing

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏去工作，把DJ台变成一个鲜活的、临时搭建的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日一闻》。

sentences.en: Today, in the coming days, a trial will begin to determine whether the fatal shooting of Ahmaud Arbery, an unarmed black man, by two armed white men,
sentences.zh: 今天，在接下来的几天里，一场审判即将开始，以判定两名武装白人男子枪杀手无寸铁的黑人男子阿莫德·阿伯里，

sentences.en: is considered murder under Georgia state law.
sentences.zh: 根据佐治亚州法律是否构成谋杀。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague Richard Fossett about why that may be a difficult case for prosecutors to make.
sentences.zh: 我与同事理查德·福塞特讨论了为什么检察官可能很难在这一案件中定罪。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月28日，星期四。

sentences.en: Richard, as we prepare for this trial to begin, I wonder if you can describe the scene at the courthouse where the trial is going to take place in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 理查德，在审判即将开始之际，我想请你描述一下佐治亚州审判所在地法院的现场情况。

sentences.en: So, this trial is taking place in the small coastal city of Brunswick, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 这场审判是在佐治亚州布伦瑞克这个小型沿海城市进行的。

sentences.en: The killing of Ahmaud Arbery took place just outside of town in a little subdivision there.
sentences.zh: 阿莫德·阿伯里的遇害地点就在城外的一个小社区里。

sentences.en: And there's just a lot of pain and anger still over what happened.
sentences.zh: 对于所发生的一切，人们心中仍有许多痛苦和愤怒。

sentences.en: And you can feel it in the voices of the people who've been gathering in front of the Glenn County courthouse.
sentences.zh: 你可以在聚集在格林县法院前的人群的声音中感受到这一点。

sentences.en: We don't want anyone to ever forget about Ahmaud.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望任何人忘记阿莫德。

sentences.en: These are local people and some people from out of state who've come.
sentences.zh: 这些人有当地居民，也有从外州赶来的民众。

sentences.en: They're chanting.
sentences.zh: 他们在高呼口号。

sentences.en: They're angry.
sentences.zh: 他们很愤怒。

sentences.en: They're hurt.
sentences.zh: 他们很受伤。

sentences.en: They're calling for justice for Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁为阿莫德·阿伯里伸张正义。

sentences.en: Twelve jurors will eventually decide the guilt or innocence of Gregory McMichael, his son Travis McMichael, and William Bryan.
sentences.zh: 十二名陪审员最终将决定格雷戈里·麦克迈克尔、他的儿子特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔以及威廉·布莱恩是否有罪。

sentences.en: You can also really feel it inside the four walls of the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 你也能在法庭内真切地感受到这种氛围。

sentences.en: The judge and attorneys are slowly and painstakingly making their way through a pool of hundreds of potential panelists.
sentences.zh: 法官和律师们正在缓慢而费力地从数百名潜在陪审员中进行筛选。

sentences.en: You've got lawyers who are having a really hard time finding locals who aren't connected to this case in some way.
sentences.zh: 律师们很难找到与此案毫无关联的当地人。

sentences.en: Brunswick, although not a small town, it's a small city, and a lot of people do know a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 布伦瑞克虽然不算小镇，但也是个小城市，很多人彼此都认识。

sentences.en: You have a number of people who've said that they know or have worked with the families of the three men accused of murder.
sentences.zh: 有很多人表示他们认识或曾与这三名被控谋杀的男子的家人共事过。

sentences.en: A number of people who said they knew Ahmaud Arbery's family.
sentences.zh: 也有不少人说他们认识阿莫德·阿伯里的家人。

sentences.en: Potential juror 247 says it would be hard for them not to be found guilty.
sentences.zh: 247号潜在陪审员表示，很难判定他们无罪。

sentences.en: It's very hard to find people who haven't formed some very strong opinions about it.
sentences.zh: 很难找到对这件事没有形成强烈观点的人。

sentences.en: All right, so we are out here now.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们现在就在外面。

sentences.en: We're in Sotilla Shores.
sentences.zh: 我们在索蒂拉海岸。

sentences.en: This is the area that Ahmaud was running through.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿莫德当时跑步经过的区域。

sentences.en: And this week, a bus drove into the Sotilla Shores neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这周，一辆巴士开进了索蒂拉海岸社区。

sentences.en: That's the subdivision where Ahmaud Arbery was gunned down.
sentences.zh: 那就是阿莫德·阿伯里被枪杀的那个社区。

sentences.en: Here we are.
sentences.zh: 我们到了。

sentences.en: I guess we're going to start walking, as you can see.
sentences.zh: 我想我们要开始步行了，如你所见。

sentences.en: The bus was full of relatives of Ahmaud and of supporters of the family.
sentences.zh: 巴士上坐满了阿莫德的亲属和支持该家庭的人们。

sentences.en: And they came to kind of have a moment of communion on this street where he was killed.
sentences.zh: 他们来到这条他遇害的街道上，进行某种形式的悼念。

sentences.en: Showing solidarity with the Ahmaud Arbery family.
sentences.zh: 以此表达对阿莫德·阿伯里一家的声援。

sentences.en: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that one of the women on the bus referred to the spot as sacred ground.
sentences.zh: 据《亚特兰大宪法报》报道，车上一名女性称这个地方为“圣地”。

sentences.en: Richard, can you remind us what happened at this spot, at what this woman describes as the sacred ground?
sentences.zh: 理查德，你能提醒我们在这个地方，也就是这位女士所说的“圣地”，到底发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we have video footage that shows a lot of what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们有视频录像显示了那天发生的大部分情况。

sentences.en: It was February 23rd, 2020.
It was a Sunday in the early afternoon.
sentences.zh: 那是一个周日的午后。

sentences.en: And we know that Ahmaud Arbery had come into the neighborhood of Sotilla Shores.
sentences.zh: 我们知道阿莫德·阿伯里当时进入了索蒂拉海岸社区。

sentences.en: There's video footage that shows him walking into a house that's under construction.
sentences.zh: 有视频录像显示他走进了一栋正在施工的房子。

sentences.en: Ahmaud lived a couple of miles away with his mom across a freeway.
sentences.zh: 阿莫德和他的母亲住在几英里外，穿过一条高速公路的地方。

sentences.en: And he was known around town as a habitual jogger.
sentences.zh: 他在镇上以经常慢跑而闻名。

sentences.en: And so it wouldn't have been weird or rare for him to be in this neighborhood on foot.
sentences.zh: 所以他步行出现在这个社区并不奇怪，也不罕见。

sentences.en: We know that he goes into this house and it's really just not clear why he's in the house.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他进了那栋房子，但确实不清楚他为什么进去。

sentences.en: He comes in, he looks around, he doesn't take anything.
sentences.zh: 他走进去，四处看了看，什么也没拿。

sentences.en: And on this particular afternoon, a neighbor across the street calls 911 and reports that Ahmaud's in the house.
sentences.zh: 就在那个下午，街对面的一位邻居拨打了911，报告说阿莫德在房子里。

sentences.en: The caller says that Ahmaud looks like a guy who's been trespassing in the area before.
sentences.zh: 报警人说阿莫德看起来像个以前在该地区非法闯入的人。

sentences.en: And this neighborhood had been, you know, very much on edge about a number of property crimes that had been occurring there.
sentences.zh: 而这个社区当时对那里发生的一系列财产犯罪非常敏感。

sentences.en: So we know that Ahmaud eventually leaves the house and he starts running down the street.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道阿莫德最终离开了房子，开始沿街奔跑。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that a neighbor named Greg McMichael, who's one of the three murder suspects in this case,
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一位名叫格雷格·麦克迈克尔的邻居，也就是本案三名谋杀嫌疑人之一，

sentences.en: he's a former police officer with the Glynn County Police Department, very much known to the kind of law enforcement apparatus there in this county.
sentences.zh: 他曾是格林县警察局的警官，在当地执法部门中非常出名。

sentences.en: He sees Ahmaud running down the street.
sentences.zh: 他看到阿莫德沿街奔跑。

sentences.en: He tells police that he grabbed his handgun and he shouted to his son, Travis McMichael, who grabbed a shotgun.
sentences.zh: 他告诉警察，他拿起了手枪，并向他的儿子特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔大喊，后者拿了一把霰弹枪。

sentences.en: And these two men jump in a pickup truck and they start chasing Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 这两个人跳上一辆皮卡车，开始追赶阿莫德·阿伯里。

sentences.en: And they say that they were screaming at him to stop, that they wanted to talk to him.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们当时冲他大喊让他停下，说他们想和他谈谈。

sentences.en: At some point, they're joined by a neighbor, William Bryan, who's the third murder suspect.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，邻居威廉·布莱恩加入了他们，他是第三名谋杀嫌疑人。

sentences.en: He's driving his own pickup truck and the chase plays out on these kind of maze-like streets in this little subdivision.
sentences.zh: 他开着自己的皮卡车，追逐战在这个小社区迷宫般的街道上展开。

sentences.en: And it ends up, video footage shows, with Greg McMichael and Travis McMichael waiting there for Ahmaud Arbery, who's kind of hemmed in now.
sentences.zh: 视频显示，最终格雷格·麦克迈克尔和特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔在那里拦截了阿莫德·阿伯里，他现在被困住了。

sentences.en: And he's approaching this pickup truck where Greg McMichael is standing in the bed of it.
sentences.zh: 他正靠近那辆皮卡车，格雷格·麦克迈克尔正站在车斗里。

sentences.en: And Travis McMichael is now standing outside of the truck, holding this shotgun.
sentences.zh: 而特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔此时正站在车外，手里拿着那把霰弹枪。

sentences.en: Travis McMichael then shoots Ahmaud Arbery and shoots again.
sentences.zh: 随后特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔向阿莫德·阿伯里开枪，又补了一枪。

sentences.en: And soon you see Ahmaud trying to run a few more steps, but he crumples there on the pavement.
sentences.zh: 很快你看到阿莫德试图再跑几步，但随后倒在了人行道上。

sentences.en: And that's where he dies.
sentences.zh: 他就在那里去世了。

sentences.en: And so the Glen County police show up to the scene.
sentences.zh: 格林县警察赶到了现场。

sentences.en: Greg McMichael, the father, is identified as a, quote, witness in this police report.
sentences.zh: 格雷格·麦克迈克尔，也就是父亲，在警方的报告中被列为所谓的“目击者”。

sentences.en: The police officer interviews him and gets his version of events, takes his statement.
sentences.zh: 警察对他进行了询问，记录了他的陈述，获取了他的证词。

sentences.en: But Greg McMichael is not arrested.
sentences.zh: 但格雷格·麦克迈克尔没有被捕。

sentences.en: Travis McMichael is not arrested.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔没有被捕。

sentences.en: William Bryan is not arrested that day.
sentences.zh: 威廉·布莱恩当天也没有被捕。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Because there's this argument that their actions are legal under George's Citizens' Arrest Law.
sentences.zh: 因为有人辩称他们的行为根据佐治亚州的“公民逮捕法”是合法的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what is that law?
sentences.zh: 那是什么法律？

sentences.en: What does it say?
sentences.zh: 它怎么规定的？

sentences.en: I'll just read this crucial part of the law.
sentences.zh: 我来读一下该法律的关键部分。

sentences.en: The law said,
sentences.zh: 法律规定，

sentences.en: A private person may arrest an offender if the offense is committed in his presence or within his immediate knowledge.
sentences.zh: 如果犯罪行为是在私人面前或其直接知情范围内发生的，私人可以逮捕犯罪者。

sentences.en: If the offense is a felony and the offender is escaping or attempting to escape, a private person may arrest him upon reasonable and probable grounds of suspicion.
sentences.zh: 如果犯罪属于重罪且犯罪者正在逃跑或试图逃跑，私人可以在有合理且可能的怀疑依据下将其逮捕。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This law dates back to 1863, to the Civil War era.
sentences.zh: 这项法律可以追溯到1863年，即内战时期。

sentences.en: And it's been criticized for helping to create an atmosphere that allowed for the extrajudicial arrest and killing of hundreds of black people in Georgia by white people during,
sentences.zh: 它一直受到批评，因为它助长了一种氛围，使得在佐治亚州历史上最黑暗的时期，

sentences.en: perhaps, the darkest period in Georgia's history.
sentences.zh: 白人可以对数百名黑人进行法外逮捕和杀害。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, this is the law that prosecutors would point to in arguing to the police that these three men should not be arrested, that they had, in fact,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，这正是检察官当时向警方指出，不应逮捕这三名男子的法律依据，他们实际上，

sentences.en: acted in accordance with this law, and that, additionally, Travis McMichael had acted in self-defense when he pulled the trigger on the argument that Ahmaud Arbery,
sentences.zh: 是按照这项法律行事的，此外，特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔在扣动扳机时是出于自卫，理由是阿莫德·阿伯里，

sentences.en: this unarmed man, had attacked him and tried to take his shotgun from him.
sentences.zh: 这个手无寸铁的人，袭击了他并试图抢夺他的霰弹枪。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So just to be clear, these three men claim, and prosecutors are accepting the claim, that this was a legally justified citizen's arrest, basically gone bad.
sentences.zh: 所以明确一下，这三名男子声称，检察官也接受了这一说法，即这是一次合法的公民逮捕，只是最终失控了。

sentences.en: That was the case for many weeks.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了好几周。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So a few months later...
sentences.zh: 几个月后……

sentences.en: This cell phone footage is believed to show Ahmaud Arbery jogging in a South Georgia neighborhood before coming upon two men in a truck.
sentences.zh: 这段手机录像被认为显示了阿莫德·阿伯里在佐治亚州南部的一个社区慢跑，随后遇到了两名坐在卡车里的男子。

sentences.en: The video of the confrontation and the killing emerges...
sentences.zh: 对峙和杀戮的视频曝光了……

sentences.en: The video, released yesterday, has brought national attention to the...
sentences.zh: 昨天发布的视频引起了全国对……的关注。

sentences.en: Filmed, in fact, by William Bryan, the third murder suspect, who was in the second pickup truck.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这段视频是由第三名谋杀嫌疑人威廉·布莱恩拍摄的，他当时就在第二辆皮卡车里。

sentences.en: A 25-year-old tries to get around them, and then...
sentences.zh: 一名25岁的年轻人试图绕过他们，然后……

sentences.en: It's horrific to watch, and I think you can say there is widespread disgust over the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 看这段视频令人毛骨悚然，我想可以说，整个事件引起了广泛的厌恶。

sentences.en: Earlier this week, I watched a video depicting Mr. Arbery's last moments alive.
sentences.zh: 本周早些时候，我观看了一段记录阿伯里先生生前最后时刻的视频。

sentences.en: I can tell you it's absolutely horrific, and Georgians deserve answers.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，这绝对令人毛骨悚然，佐治亚州人民理应得到答案。

sentences.en: And I remember, as it was all exploding, a Republican source of mine here in Georgia saying something like,
sentences.zh: 我记得，当这一切爆发时，我在佐治亚州的一位共和党消息人士曾说，

sentences.en: My Twitter feed is full of ultra-conservative white Georgia Republicans, and they're all totally repulsed by all this.
sentences.zh: 我的推特动态里全是极度保守的佐治亚州白人共和党人，他们对这一切感到完全反感。

sentences.en: First District Congressman Buddy Carter is reacting to the case, saying in part that the community is rightfully shaken and on edge,
sentences.zh: 第一选区国会议员巴迪·卡特对此案作出回应，称社区理所当然地感到震惊和不安，

sentences.en: and the video footage and what's been reported is deeply troubling, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，视频录像和报道的内容令人深感不安。

sentences.en: You know, no one can look at the Arbery video and not come to the conclusion that this was hate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有人能看完阿伯里的视频而不得出这是仇恨犯罪的结论。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, we have the killing of George Floyd, another unarmed black man, and a lot of outrage emerging over the treatment of black people in this country.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，乔治·弗洛伊德——另一名手无寸铁的黑人男子——被杀，国内对黑人所受待遇的愤怒情绪高涨。

sentences.en: And in Georgia, in a state where it's very difficult to get lawmakers and people on two sides of this political divide to agree on anything,
sentences.zh: 而在佐治亚州，在这个很难让立法者和政治分歧双方在任何事情上达成一致的州，

sentences.en: You saw something really incredible start to happen,
sentences.zh: 你看到了一些真正不可思议的事情开始发生，

sentences.en: and that is this series of decisions to really profoundly alter Georgia's criminal code as a result of the killing of Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 那就是一系列旨在深刻改变佐治亚州刑法的决定，而这一切都是阿莫德·阿伯里遇害的结果。

sentences.en: The first big change comes when the Republican-dominated state legislature, at the request of Governor Kemp,
sentences.zh: 第一个重大变化出现在共和党主导的州议会，应肯普州长的要求，

sentences.en: starts drawing up what would be Georgia's first ever hate crimes law.
sentences.zh: 开始起草佐治亚州有史以来第一部仇恨犯罪法。

sentences.en: Georgia at the time was one of only four states that did not have a state hate crimes law.
sentences.zh: 当时的佐治亚州是仅有的四个没有州级仇恨犯罪法的州之一。

sentences.en: Good afternoon, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家下午好。

sentences.en: This is certainly an unprecedented moment in our state.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是我们州前所未有的时刻。

sentences.en: Brian Kemp, one of the most conservative Republican governors in the country, ends up signing this bill into law in June of 2020.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·肯普，全国最保守的共和党州长之一，最终在2020年6月签署了这项法案。

sentences.en: Georgians protested to demand action, and state lawmakers rose to the occasion.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州人民抗议要求采取行动，州议员们也挺身而出。

sentences.en: And he was very explicit at the time that this was a response to the Ahmaud Arbery killing.
sentences.zh: 他在当时非常明确地表示，这是对阿莫德·阿伯里遇害事件的回应。

sentences.en: And in fact, at the time, and I'll quote him, he called the killing a horrific, hate-filled act of violence.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时他称这次杀戮为“一场可怕的、充满仇恨的暴力行为”。

sentences.en: We saw injustice with our own eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们亲眼目睹了不公正。

sentences.en: But that wasn't all.
sentences.zh: 但这还不是全部。

sentences.en: Today we are replacing a Civil War-era law right for abuse.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们正在废除一项容易被滥用的内战时期法律。

sentences.en: What we subsequently saw, again, at Mr. Kemp's request, was the state legislature moving to make serious changes to this controversial citizen's arrest law.
sentences.zh: 随后，我们再次看到在肯普先生的要求下，州议会采取行动，对这项有争议的“公民逮捕法”进行了重大修改。

sentences.en: To root out injustice and set our state on a better path forward.
sentences.zh: 以根除不公正，引领我们的州走上更好的道路。

sentences.en: Once again, this bill received tremendous bipartisan support in the Republican-controlled legislature.
sentences.zh: 再一次，这项法案在共和党控制的议会中获得了巨大的两党支持。

sentences.en: And these changes effectively gutted the citizen's arrest law,
sentences.zh: 这些修改实际上废除了“公民逮捕法”的核心，

sentences.en: removing a lot of the language that was initially used to justify the actions of these three white men outside of Brunswick at the beginning of 2020.
sentences.zh: 删除了许多最初被用来为2020年初布伦瑞克外那三名白人男子的行为辩护的措辞。

sentences.en: We are honored to have Ahmaud's mother, Ms. Wanda Cooper-Jones, and his sister join us today.
sentences.zh: 我们很荣幸今天能邀请到阿莫德的母亲万达·库珀-琼斯女士和他的妹妹参加。

sentences.en: On behalf of all Georgians, I want to thank you both for being here.
sentences.zh: 我谨代表所有佐治亚州人民，感谢你们两位的到来。

sentences.en: There was some sense that something remarkable had happened here that you don't often see after one of these horrific events.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，这里发生了一些非同寻常的事情，这在这些可怕事件发生后并不常见。

sentences.en: And that is, even though a lot of people call for substantive change after these kinds of things, you don't always see it.
sentences.zh: 那就是，尽管很多人在这些事情发生后呼吁实质性的改变，但你并不总能看到它。

sentences.en: And in this case, we actually saw it.
sentences.zh: 而在本案中，我们确实看到了。

sentences.en: We saw real, tangible, legal change.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了真正、具体、法律层面的改变。

sentences.en: But what's really interesting as we approach opening statements in this trial is that all of these important and substantive changes are really likely to have very little effect on the outcome.
sentences.zh: 但真正有趣的是，随着我们进入本案的开庭陈述阶段，所有这些重要且实质性的改变很可能对结果影响甚微。

sentences.en: And the question of whether or not these three men are innocent or guilty in the murder of Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 以及这三名男子在谋杀阿莫德·阿伯里一案中是否有罪的问题。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，每晚你都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个鲜活的、临时搭建的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日通讯《DealBook》的商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将采访一些在商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人，将亲临纽约市 DealBook 峰会的舞台。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日于 NYTimes.com 进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Richard, why would all of these changes to the law in Georgia, and culturally, with all these expressions of revulsion over what happened to Ahmaud Arbery,
sentences.zh: 理查德，为什么佐治亚州法律的所有这些变化，以及在文化上，伴随着对阿莫德·阿伯里遭遇的种种愤慨表达，

sentences.en: why would none of that be reflected in the trial of these three men who have been accused of murdering Arbery?
sentences.zh: 为什么这一切都没有反映在这三名被控谋杀阿伯里的男子的审判中呢？

sentences.en: It's because of the fact that in our legal system, the law that applies when you go to court is the law that existed at the time of the incidents in question.
sentences.zh: 这是因为在我们的法律体系中，当你上法庭时适用的法律，是事件发生时所存在的法律。

sentences.en: And so what we have is, in the case of the old citizen's arrest law, a law that, even though it's not in the books, will be used as a pillar in the defense strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在的情况是，就旧的公民逮捕法而言，尽管它已不再适用，但它仍将被用作辩护策略的支柱。

sentences.en: And when it comes to the hate crimes law, these three men can't be charged under it because that law didn't exist at the time that they committed these acts.
sentences.zh: 而谈到仇恨犯罪法时，这三个人无法据此被起诉，因为在他们实施这些行为时，该法律尚不存在。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So for the purposes of this trial, the only thing that matters is what the law said on the day that Ahmaud Arbery was killed.
sentences.zh: 因此，就本次审判而言，唯一重要的是阿莫德·阿伯里被杀当天法律的规定。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And think about this.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: You know, here is this horrific act.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一起骇人听闻的事件。

sentences.en: It spurs landmark legislative change, and yet none of it really applies.
sentences.zh: 它促成了具有里程碑意义的立法变革，然而这些变革实际上并不适用。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It's just, it's a really, it's like no case I've ever covered.
sentences.zh: 这真的，这就像我报道过的任何案件都不一样。

sentences.en: And so if these existing laws of February 2020 are the laws under which this case will be tried, what does that mean for the defense?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果 2020 年 2 月现行的法律是本案审判所依据的法律，这对辩方意味着什么？

sentences.en: How do we expect them to make their case with those laws being their North Star?
sentences.zh: 我们如何指望他们以这些法律为准绳来进行辩护？

sentences.en: Well, there are a few things in talking to the defense teams in this case that are worth noting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在与本案辩护团队交谈时，有几点值得注意。

sentences.en: One of them is the fact that they believe, and they're going to argue, that this case really had nothing to do with race or racism at all.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他们相信，并且他们会辩称，这起案件实际上与种族或种族主义毫无关系。

sentences.en: That it was a well-meaning attempt to keep the peace in a neighborhood that had been troubled by a bunch of property crimes.
sentences.zh: 这只是为了在一个饱受财产犯罪困扰的社区中维持治安的善意尝试。

sentences.en: And flowing from that is this idea that the citizen's arrest law should protect these guys and that they should be seen as people who are trying to effectuate an arreSt.
sentences.zh: 由此引申出的观点是，公民逮捕法应该保护这些人，他们应该被视为试图实施逮捕的人。

sentences.en: And then that's going to be tied with this argument that the shooting was an act of self-defense.
sentences.zh: 然后，这将与枪击是正当防卫行为的论点联系在一起。

sentences.en: Ahmaud Arbery, this unarmed man, chased down by three men, two of whom were armed, was in fact the aggressor in this case,
sentences.zh: 阿莫德·阿伯里，这个手无寸铁的人，被三名男子追赶，其中两人持有武器，实际上才是本案的侵略者，

sentences.en: based on the defense's assertion that Ahmaud tried to grab Travis McMichael's shotgun.
sentences.zh: 这是基于辩方声称阿莫德试图抢夺特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔的猎枪。

sentences.en: We think they're going to say that Travis McMichael was, at that point, authorized to use deadly force in self-defense.
sentences.zh: 我们认为他们会说，特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔在当时有权使用致命武力进行自卫。

sentences.en: And I think for a lot of people, it's going to bring to mind the 2012 incident in which George Zimmerman, the Florida Neighborhood Watch volunteer,
sentences.zh: 我想对很多人来说，这会让人想起 2012 年发生的事件，当时佛罗里达州社区守望志愿者乔治·齐默尔曼，

sentences.en: engaged with yet another unarmed black male, Trayvon Martin.
sentences.zh: 与另一名手无寸铁的黑人男性特雷沃恩·马丁发生了冲突。

sentences.en: That case went to trial in 2013.
sentences.zh: 那起案件在 2013 年进行了审判。

sentences.en: I think it was a second-degree murder and manslaughter trial.
sentences.zh: 我想那是一场二级谋杀和过失杀人罪的审判。

sentences.en: And Mr. Zimmerman beat it.
sentences.zh: 齐默尔曼先生胜诉了。

sentences.en: He was acquitted.
sentences.zh: 他被判无罪。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of parallels.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: In fact, I talked to Marco Mara, who was probably the best-known lawyer who was working on the defense for Mr. Zimmerman.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我采访了马可·马拉，他可能是为齐默尔曼先生辩护的最著名的律师。

sentences.en: And he thinks that these guys have a good case.
sentences.zh: 他认为这些人有很好的辩护理由。

sentences.en: And he also pointed out some of the really parallels here that are just very difficult to escape.
sentences.zh: 他还指出了一些非常难以回避的相似之处。

sentences.en: Here you have two cases of people arguing that they were not involved in some kind of racist hunting down of a person, but they were trying to protect their neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这里有两起案件，人们都辩称他们没有参与某种针对个人的种族主义猎杀，而是在试图保护他们的社区。

sentences.en: You also have the self-defense case that's going to be put forth by an armed person claiming that they were threatened by the unarmed person that they were tailing.
sentences.zh: 你还有武装人员提出的正当防卫辩护，声称他们受到了所跟踪的非武装人员的威胁。

sentences.en: So he thinks that could be a successful legal strategy for these three guys in the same way it was for George Zimmerman.
sentences.zh: 所以他认为，这对于这三个人来说可能是一种成功的法律策略，就像对乔治·齐默尔曼一样。

sentences.en: What's strange about that defense is that it turns people walking down the street, whether it's Trayvon Martin or Ahmaud Arbery,
sentences.zh: 这种辩护奇怪的地方在于，它把走在街上的人，无论是特雷沃恩·马丁还是阿莫德·阿伯里，

sentences.en: into aggressors for responding to armed men who suddenly are pursuing them.
sentences.zh: 变成了对突然追赶他们的武装人员做出反应的侵略者。

sentences.en: And it says that the right to self-defense of those pursuers is greater than the right to self-defense of these two men walking down the street.
sentences.zh: 并且它声称，这些追赶者的正当防卫权利大于这两个走在街上的人的正当防卫权利。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's exactly the critique that a lot of people who would like to see a guilty verdict in this case would bring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这正是许多希望看到本案有罪判决的人会提出的批评。

sentences.en: And yeah,
sentences.zh: 而且是的，

sentences.en: that is this sense that it is arguably nothing other than patently absurd to assume that an unarmed black man running through a deep south neighborhood pursued by white guys with guns could in any universe be considered an aggressor.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉是，假设一个手无寸铁的黑人男子在深南部的社区奔跑，被持枪的白人追赶，在任何情况下都可能被视为侵略者，这简直是荒谬至极。

sentences.en: But I think what the defense attorneys are going to do here is hope that the jury applies a very close reading of the law to that very moment where these two men begin this altercation on the hopes that they determine that there would be a threat to the lives of these white men that justified the use of deadly force.
sentences.zh: 但我认为辩护律师在这里要做的是，希望陪审团对这两个人开始冲突的那一刻进行非常仔细的法律解读，希望他们认定这些白人的生命受到了威胁，从而证明使用致命武力的合理性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It seems like the prosecution is going to have to wrestle with this citizen's arrest law as it was written originally and as it was in place when Ahmaud Arbery was killed at some point in this trial.
sentences.zh: 看起来控方在审判的某个阶段将不得不与这项最初编写并于阿莫德·阿伯里被杀时生效的公民逮捕法进行博弈。

sentences.en: Do you have any sense of how the prosecution plans to talk about it and to rebut the defense's argument that these three men were following that law?
sentences.zh: 你是否了解控方打算如何谈论它，以及如何反驳辩方关于这三个人是在遵循该法律的论点？

sentences.en: Well, in some of the prosecution's filings,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在控方的一些文件中，

sentences.en: we see what appears to be an argument that's going to push back against the idea that this old citizen's arrest law should have been applied at all.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了似乎是一个要反驳这种旧的公民逮捕法根本不应该适用的论点。

sentences.en: That law said, again, that a private person may arrest an offender if the offense is committed in his presence or within his immediate knowledge,
sentences.zh: 该法律再次规定，如果犯罪行为是在其面前或在其直接知情范围内发生的，私人可以逮捕罪犯，

sentences.en: and the offense also has to be a felony.
sentences.zh: 而且该犯罪行为还必须是重罪。

sentences.en: So, in court filings, you have prosecutors saying that Ahmaud Arbery was chased down by men who were attempting to unlawfully detain him, even though, as they write,
sentences.zh: 所以，在法庭文件中，检察官说阿莫德·阿伯里是被试图非法拘留他的人追赶的，尽管正如他们所写，

sentences.en: these men had not seen Mr. Arbery commit any crime on February 23rd of 2020.
sentences.zh: 这些人并没有看到阿伯里先生在 2020 年 2 月 23 日犯下任何罪行。

sentences.en: And they had no knowledge of any felony offense he had committed.
sentences.zh: 而且他们对所犯的任何重罪一无所知。

sentences.en: I think prosecutors are also going to push back rather hard against the idea that Ahmaud Arbery was the aggressor.
sentences.zh: 我认为检察官也会非常强烈地反驳阿莫德·阿伯里是侵略者的观点。

sentences.en: They also write about how Ahmaud at that moment was unable to escape what prosecutors called, quote, the strange men who were chasing him.
sentences.zh: 他们还写道，阿莫德在那一刻无法逃脱检察官所称的“追赶他的陌生人”。

sentences.en: And that Ahmaud Arbery had nowhere to run.
sentences.zh: 而且阿莫德·阿伯里无处可逃。

sentences.en: He was hemmed in by William Bryan's truck, which he was running away from, and he was running right into the trouble of the McMichaels.
sentences.zh: 他被威廉·布莱恩的卡车围住了，他正从卡车那里跑开，却直接跑进了麦克迈克尔一家的麻烦中。

sentences.en: And at that moment, when he veers around the side of the truck, he is, according to this argument, facing two possibilities, to confront the man with the shotgun,
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，当他绕过卡车侧面时，根据这一论点，他面临两种可能：面对那个拿着猎枪的人，

sentences.en: who is now standing a few feet away from him, or to turn his back on that man and risk being shot in the back.
sentences.zh: 那个人现在离他只有几英尺远，或者背对着那个人，冒着被从背后射杀的风险。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But in general,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，

sentences.en: I think the people who are watching this case closely think that the prosecution is going to also have to hope that a jury looks beyond just these very specific moments.
sentences.zh: 我认为密切关注此案的人认为，控方也将不得不希望陪审团不仅要看这些非常具体的时刻。

sentences.en: And one thing that seems likely to come up in this case is the issue of race and the issue of racism.
sentences.zh: 本案中可能出现的一个问题是种族和种族主义问题。

sentences.en: A number of months ago, there was a Georgia Bureau of Investigation agent who testified that William Bryan, the third murder suspect in the second truck,
sentences.zh: 几个月前，有一名佐治亚州调查局的探员作证说，第二辆卡车里的第三名谋杀嫌疑人威廉·布莱恩，

sentences.en: heard Travis McMichael use a racist slur shortly after he shot and killed Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 在特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔开枪打死阿莫德·阿伯里后不久，听到了他使用了种族歧视的侮辱性词汇。

sentences.en: And this same agent has also said that there were text messages and social media posts in which Travis McMichael used racial epithets.
sentences.zh: 而同一位探员也表示，特拉维斯·麦克迈克尔在短信和社交媒体帖子中使用了种族歧视的称呼。

sentences.en: So that could be the basis, in theory,
sentences.zh: 所以从理论上讲，这可能成为，

sentences.en: for a prosecutorial argument that the real motive here was racism and not a citizen's arrest seeking to detain someone who these men thought committed a burglary.
sentences.zh: 控方论点的基础，即这里的真正动机是种族主义，而不是为了拘留他们认为犯了入室盗窃罪的人而进行的公民逮捕。

sentences.en: I think there's just this very good chance that these kinds of issues are going to be introduced at trial.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些问题很有可能在审判中被提出来。

sentences.en: And I don't know exactly how, but I think it's going to make for some very painful and very explosive moments over the course of this thing.
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体会怎样，但我认为这会让整个过程中出现一些非常痛苦和非常爆炸性的时刻。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: But, Richard, if the jury does end up supporting the defense argument that under the original law, the unchanged law, everything that happened here was legal,
sentences.zh: 但是，理查德，如果陪审团最终支持辩方的论点，即根据原始法律，即未修改的法律，这里发生的一切都是合法的，

sentences.en: what will that mean, and what will it mean to the people you saw standing in front of the courthouse or the people who went to visit that site and called it sacred ground?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？对于你在法院前看到的那些人，或者那些去过现场并称其为圣地的人来说，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: That's such a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And in some ways, if there is an acquittal in this case, it's going to feel like a rerun of these certain kinds of cases.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，如果本案被判无罪，那会让人感觉像是某些特定案件的重演。

sentences.en: Another case wherein it appears that the people on trial exercised at least spectacularly poor judgment and committed acts that many people would, in fact,
sentences.zh: 又一起案件，其中受审的人似乎表现出了极其糟糕的判断力，并做出了许多人实际上会，

sentences.en: find to be morally unconscionable.
sentences.zh: 认为在道德上不可接受的行为。

sentences.en: But, nonetheless, it could end up being determined that what they did was not technically illegal.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，最终可能被认定他们的行为在技术上并不违法。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: And it's a very—it's a very—it could be a very bitter pill for people to swallow.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常——这是一个非常——这可能是一个让人们难以接受的苦果。

sentences.en: And do you think that that pill is more bitter, given the political changes that have happened in Georgia since Ahmaud Arbery and because of Ahmaud Arbery,
sentences.zh: 你认为考虑到阿莫德·阿伯里之后以及因为阿莫德·阿伯里而在佐治亚州发生的政治变化，这个苦果是否更苦，

sentences.en: or might that make this pill less bitter because those changes have at least occurred?
sentences.zh: 还是说因为这些变化至少已经发生，这会让苦果不那么苦？

sentences.en: I just don't even know how to measure the bitterness.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道该如何衡量这种苦涩。

sentences.en: When you're down there in Brunswick, Georgia, you're reminded that this young man is dead and he died before he could find a life partner, before he could have children.
sentences.zh: 当你身处佐治亚州布伦瑞克时，你会想起这个年轻人已经死了，他在找到人生伴侣之前，在拥有孩子之前就去世了。

sentences.en: That he has no opportunity to mature and to grow old.
sentences.zh: 他没有机会成熟和变老。

sentences.en: The pain is immeasurable, and I just don't know if any change to any law can really kind of serve as a balm for that kind of pain.
sentences.zh: 痛苦是无法衡量的，我不知道任何法律的任何改变是否真的能成为那种痛苦的慰藉。

sentences.en: That justice for them in the political sphere may not be enough if they're not able to get it themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果他们自己无法获得正义，那么他们在政治领域获得的正义可能是不够的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just don't know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, a young man is dead and he's not coming back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个年轻人死了，他再也回不来了。

sentences.en: Richard, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 理查德，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The murder trial is expected to begin as soon as next week.
sentences.zh: 谋杀案审判预计最早将于下周开始。

sentences.en: Regardless of the outcome, the three men accused of killing Ahmaud Arbery will face a second trial next year on federal charges of hate crimes.
sentences.zh: 无论结果如何，被控杀害阿莫德·阿伯里的三名男子明年将面临第二场审判，罪名是联邦仇恨犯罪。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜总会担任 DJ 的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都会带着 300 件最珍贵的财产去工作，你会把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在您最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要知道的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Wednesday night, Democratic lawmakers had yet to reach an agreement on what should be included in a major social spending bill or even how to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，民主党议员尚未就一项重大社会支出法案应包含的内容，甚至如何为其提供资金达成一致。

sentences.en: Democrats remain at odds over several key measures, such as expanding access to health care in states that refuse to adopt the Affordable Care Act
sentences.zh: 民主党人在几项关键措施上仍存在分歧，例如在拒绝采用《平价医疗法案》的州扩大医疗保健的获取途径，

sentences.en: and offering paid family and medical leave to millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 并为数百万美国人提供带薪家庭和医疗假。

sentences.en: In a new setback,
sentences.zh: 在一次新的挫折中，

sentences.en: Senator Joe Manchin of West Virginia said he opposed both the paid leave plan and a popular proposal for funding much of the bill by taxing the country's billionaires,
sentences.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州参议员乔·曼钦表示，他反对带薪休假计划，也反对通过对国家亿万富翁征税来资助该法案大部分内容的流行提案，

sentences.en: a proposal that Manchin said he found unfair.
sentences.zh: 曼钦称该提案是不公平的。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Diana Wynn, Lindsay Garrison, and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由戴安娜·韦恩、琳赛·加里森和埃里克·克鲁普克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow, with help from Paige Coward, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music from Marion Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周编辑，佩奇·考沃德协助，克里斯·伍德担任工程设计，并包含玛丽昂·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰德弗克创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Emily Cochran.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢艾米丽·科克伦。

sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。
